acceptance_criteria: A dispatched worker commits, pushes and opens its own pull request without the Product Owner finishing it.
The writable roots contain the object store and nothing broader.
The orchestrator suite and the repository privacy gate pass.

baseline.authority: docs/design/GOV_PO_3_APPROVED_MOVEMENT_ORCHESTRATION.md (FROZEN) fixes the worktree-per-movement dispatch model. PR #371 removed the first half of the reason that model could not complete; this movement removes the second.
baseline.observed: Movement NXS-LOCAL-0217 ran after #371 and #376 merged. Its compile step passed, its privacy gate passed, and it still could not commit. Its own closing words: Restore Git object-store write access, then commit and open the PR.
baseline.what_exists:
A commit writes two places. The index and its lock live in the worktree's own directory, which #371 already opens:

  git -C <worktree> rev-parse --git-dir
  <main repo>/.git/worktrees/NXS-LOCAL-0217

The objects it writes do not. They go to the shared store under the main repository's .git/objects, which no writable root covers.

scripts/orchestrator.py:1017 defines _add_engineer_toolchains and the git directory is added around scripts/orchestrator.py:1111, per #371. The object store is a sibling of .git/worktrees, not a child of it, so deriving it from the worktree git directory means walking to the common directory rather than composing a path.

invariants: No engineer gains write access to refs, to config, or to another movement's worktree state.
report.merge_gate: The worker opens the pull request and does not merge it. If it opens its own pull request, that is itself the acceptance evidence.
report.objective: A dispatched worker can complete a commit. PR #371 opened its worktree's index directory; a commit also writes objects, and that store is elsewhere.
output_contract: A SESSION CLOSE on the relay as one NEXUS_SESSION_PACKET.

recommended_reasoning.reason: One derived path added to an existing list, with the boundary already reasoned and the wrong broader answer named.

requirements: Grant the object store and nothing adjacent to it. Objects are content-addressed and effectively append-only, which is why this grant is defensible where a grant of refs would not be. Say that reasoning in the pull request so the next reader knows where the line is.
Derive, do not compose. A repository can be configured with a relocated object directory or with alternates.
risks: Reaching for .git wholesale would make every movement able to move another lane's refs. The narrower grant is the whole point of doing this as its own movement rather than widening #371 after the fact.

in: Add the repository's shared object store to the sandbox writable roots for a dispatched engineer, derived from git rather than composed from a parent path.

Derive it the way git itself names it. git rev-parse --git-common-dir gives the shared directory; the object store is what git reports beneath it, and an alternates or a relocated objects directory must not break the derivation.
A test that fails if the writable roots omit the object store for a linked worktree.
out: Granting the whole shared .git directory. Refs, config and other worktrees' state live there, and one movement must not be able to touch another's.
Moving to a permissive sandbox mode.
Changing the merge gate, the relay protocol or the dispatch model.

changed: Added Git-derived object-store writable root via git rev-parse --git-path=objects.
Extended the named Codex spawn test for the object-store root.

effects.main_py: Dispatched Codex engineers receive only the Git-reported object store in addition to existing narrow roots.
